source_text:
de Resurrectione
Περὶ τοῦ Λαζάρου καὶ τοῦ πλουσίου ἀπορεῖσθαι δύναται· τῶν μὲν ἁπλουστέρων
οἰομένων ταῦτα λελέχθαι, ὡς ἀμφοτέρων μετὰ τῶν σωμάτων λαμβανόντων τὰ ἄξια
τῶν τῷ βίῳ πεπραγμένων· τῶν δὲ ἀκριβεστέρων, ἐπεὶ μετὰ τὴν ἀνάστασιν οὐδεὶς ἐν
βίῳ καταλείπεται, οὐκ ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει οἰομένων ταῦτα γεγονέναι· λέγει γὰρ ὁ
πλούσιος, ὅτι «πέντε ἀδελφοὺς ἔχω, καὶ ἵνα μὴ ἔλθωσιν εἰς τὸν τόπον τοῦτον τῆς
βασάνου, πέμψον Λάζαρον ἀπαγγέλλοντα αὐτοῖς τὰ ἐνταῦθα·» καὶ διὰ τούτων
ζητούντων τὴν γλῶσσαν, καὶ τὸν δάκτυλον, καὶ τοὺς κόλπους Ἀβραὰμ, καὶ τὴν
ἀνάκλισιν.
thought_title: Two readings of the parable of Lazarus and the rich man
orientation: Origen opens the treatise by laying out a disputed question about the parable of Lazarus and the rich man, distinguishing simpler readers from more precise ones.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning Lazarus and the rich man it is possible to be at a loss. On the one hand the simpler ones think that these things have been said as both of them with their bodies receiving the things worthy of the things done in life. [Two interpretive groups: the simpler readers and the more precise readers.] On the other hand the more precise ones, since after the resurrection no one is left behind in life, think that these things have not happened in the resurrection. [Two interpretive groups: the simpler readers and the more precise readers.] For the rich man says that "I have five brothers, and so that they may not come into this place of torment, send Lazarus to report to them the things here." And through these things they seek the tongue, and the finger, and the bosom of Abraham, and the reclining.

choices.english: it is possible to be at a loss
choices.why: Keeps the impersonal construction and the sense of a genuine open question, matching the treatise's disputed-question framing.

choices.english: On the one hand the simpler ones
choices.why: Preserves the μὲν...δὲ contrast between the two groups of readers, which structures the whole section.

choices.term: τὰ ἄξια τῶν τῷ βίῳ πεπραγμένων
choices.english: the things worthy of the things done in life
choices.why: Literal rendering keeps the genitive of the things done and the adjective 'worthy' governing them, preserving the awkwardness of the Greek.
rejected: what they deserve for what they did in life
the due rewards of their deeds in life

choices.term: ἐπεὶ μετὰ τὴν ἀνάστασιν οὐδεὶς ἐν βίῳ καταλείπεται
choices.english: since after the resurrection no one is left behind in life
choices.why: Keeps the causal ἐπεὶ and the passive 'is left behind,' which is the precise readers' stated reason for denying the parable is about the resurrection.
rejected: since after the resurrection no one remains alive
because after the resurrection no one is left in this life

choices.term: πέμψον Λάζαρον ἀπαγγέλλοντα αὐτοῖς τὰ ἐνταῦθα
choices.english: send Lazarus to report to them the things here
choices.why: Keeps the participle 'reporting' and the adverb 'here,' preserving the direct quotation's force and the rich man's reference to his present location.
rejected: send Lazarus to tell them about this place
send Lazarus to announce to them what is here

choices.why: The genitive absolute continues the more precise readers' action; rendering it as a finite verb keeps the flow clear while preserving the source's participial structure in the gloss.

pass_b_english: A question can be raised about Lazarus and the rich man. The simpler readers think these words were spoken because both men receive, together with their bodies, what their deeds in life deserve. The more precise readers, however, do not think these events occurred in the resurrection, since after the resurrection no one remains in this life. For the rich man says, "I have five brothers; send Lazarus to report to them what happens here, so that they do not come into this place of torment." And through these words they inquire into the tongue, the finger, Abraham's bosom, and the reclining.

problems.source_quote: λέγει γὰρ ὁ πλούσιος, ὅτι «πέντε ἀδελφοὺς ἔχω...»
problems.why: The quotation conflates Luke 16:27-28; 'send Lazarus' is v.27, 'I have five brothers' is v.28. Single verse citation is inaccurate.
problems.ruling: Quotation conflates Luke 16:27 ('send Lazarus') and 16:28 ('five brothers'); single citation misleads.

problems.source_quote: πέντε ἀδελφοὺς ἔχω, καὶ ἵνα μὴ ἔλθωσιν εἰς τὸν τόπον τοῦτον τῆς βασάνου, πέμψον Λάζαρον ἀπαγγέλλοντα αὐτοῖς τὰ ἐνταῦθα
problems.why: The quoted words match Luke 16:27-28 closely but the source citation in brief says Luke 16:19-31 for the parable. The English adds a scripture reference not in the source text. However, the brief says 'Origen refers to' these passages. The English supplies a reference. Is this an error? The source text does not contain '(Luke 16:27-28)'. This is an addition by the translator. But the brief says scripture references should use LXX names. Luke is not LXX. However, this is a New Testament reference. The brief says 'LXX book names and Psalm numbering should be used, with modern equivalents noted where they differ.' For NT, standard names apply. But the main issue: the English adds a scripture citation not in the source. Is this an 'addition'? The source quotes the rich man without citing Luke. The English adds '(Luke 16:27-28)'. This is editorial addition not in source.
problems.fix: Remove '(Luke 16:27-28)' or verify if editorial additions are permitted.
problems.ruling: Source has no scripture citation; English adds '(Luke 16:27-28)' not in Greek text, misleading readers into thinking Origen cited it.

fixed: Removed the added scripture reference '(Luke 16:27-28)' because it is not in the source text.

problems.quote: and so that they do not come
problems.why: The rich man's quote lacks 'send Lazarus' imperative force in context; but more critically, 'and so that' for καὶ ἵνα is odd. The καὶ connects to previous clause, ἵνα μὴ = 'so that...not.' The quote is truncated: missing 'send Lazarus' as main verb. Actually checking: πέμψον Λάζαρον is imperative 'send Lazarus'—but English has 'send Lazarus' later. The structure 'I have five brothers, and so that... send Lazarus' is garbled. Should be 'I have five brothers; send Lazarus, so that they do not come...'
problems.fix: I have five brothers; send Lazarus to report to them the things here, so that they do not come into this place of torment
problems.ruling: πέμψον Λάζαρον is imperative; English 'I have five brothers, and so that...send Lazarus' garbles syntax into 'I have brothers, and so that they don't come, send Lazarus'—confusing.

problems.quote: And through these words they seek
problems.why: Greek has genitive absolute/participle continuing 'the more precise readers' as subject: 'and as they seek through these things...' English 'they seek' loses the participial connection to the precise readers; but worse, 'through these words' for διὰ τούτων is wrong—τούτων refers back to the details mentioned (tongue, finger, etc.), not 'words.' 'Through these things' or 'by these details.'
problems.fix: And by these details they seek
problems.ruling: διὰ τούτων refers to the details (tongue, finger, κόλπους), not 'words'; 'these words' misleads reader about what precise readers investigate.

edits.old: I have five brothers, and so that they do not come into this place of torment, send Lazarus to report to them the things here.
edits.new: I have five brothers; send Lazarus to report to them the things here, so that they do not come into this place of torment.

edits.old: And through these words they seek
edits.new: And by these details they seek

problems.quote: The simpler readers think these words were spoken because both men receive, together with their bodies, what their deeds in life deserve.
problems.why: Author's view or reported view? 'Simpler' seems dismissive but author may agree with bodily resurrection
problems.fix: Add 'According to some' or clarify author sides with bodily resurrection

problems.why: Two interpretive groups named only here; reader cannot tell who they represent.
problems.fix: Briefly identify both groups (e.g., two interpretive traditions).

edits.old: The simpler readers think these words were spoken because both men receive, together with their bodies, what their deeds in life deserve.
edits.new: According to the simpler readers, these words were spoken because both men receive, together with their bodies, what their deeds in life deserve.

edits.old: The more precise readers, however, deny that these events occurred in the resurrection, since after the resurrection no one remains in this life.
edits.new: According to the more precise readers, however, these events did not occur in the resurrection, since after the resurrection no one remains in this life.

fixed: The speaker problem is real: the English presented the simpler readers' view as the author's own. Added 'According to' to mark it as a reported view.
The glossary problem is real: the two interpretive groups were not identified. Added a bracketed note in the gloss identifying both groups.

problems.quote: And from these details the more precise readers point to the tongue, the finger, Abraham's bosom, and the reclining.
problems.source_quote: καὶ διὰ τούτων ζητούντων τὴν γλῶσσαν, καὶ τὸν δάκτυλον, καὶ τοὺς κόλπους Ἀβραὰμ, καὶ τὴν ἀνάκλισιν.
problems.why: ζητούντων means 'inquiring into/seeking' (what tongue, finger, bosom, reclining mean), not 'point to'. The source continues the sentence as an inquiry, not an assertion by the readers.
problems.fix: And through these words they ask about the tongue, the finger, Abraham's bosom, and the reclining.

edits.old: And from these details the more precise readers point to the tongue, the finger, Abraham's bosom, and the reclining.
edits.new: And through these words they inquire into the tongue, the finger, Abraham's bosom, and the reclining.

fixed: Changed 'point to' to 'inquire into' to correctly translate ζητούντων as seeking/inquiring (what these details signify), not asserting; 'the more precise readers' replaced with 'they' to follow the Greek genitive absolute construction without adding a subject not in the source; 'details' changed to 'words' to match διὰ τούτων referring to the rich man's statement.

polish.changed: Clarified the two groups of readers, smoothed the double 'things' phrasing, corrected 'seek' to 'point to,' and made the final 'they' explicitly refer to the more precise readers.

notes.why: Greek likely akribesteros; 'precise' readers are skeptics, not careful exegetes

notes.quote: they seek the tongue, and the finger, and Abraham's bosom, and the reclining
notes.why: 'Seek' is wrong verb; they 'find' or 'use' these details as evidence

notes.quote: both receive, together with their bodies, the things worthy of the things done in life
notes.why: Double 'things' is clumsy; 'rewards/punishments fitting their deeds' intended
notes.fix: both receive, along with their bodies, recompense fitting their deeds

notes.quote: And by these details they seek the tongue, and the finger, and Abraham's bosom, and the reclining.
notes.why: 'They' is ambiguous—refers to 'the more precise readers' but across a long sentence.

polish.changed: Clarified that both interpretations are reported views, not the author's own claim; made the contrast between the two groups clearer; kept all details and the Scripture quotation intact.

notes.quote: the tongue, the finger, Abraham's bosom, and the reclining
notes.why: Bodily details from Luke 16:24, 22 unexplained; modern reader lacks context
notes.fix: Add note: 'rich man's tongue, Lazarus's finger, dining posture'

notes.quote: The simpler readers think these words were spoken because both men receive, together with their bodies, what their deeds in life deserve.
notes.why: Author's view or reported view? 'Simpler' seems dismissive but author may agree with bodily resurrection
notes.fix: Add 'According to some' or clarify author sides with bodily resurrection

notes.why: Two interpretive groups named only here; reader cannot tell who they represent.
notes.fix: Briefly identify both groups (e.g., two interpretive traditions).

notes.why: Technical term for paradise/intermediate state; unexplained for modern reader.
notes.fix: Gloss as 'the resting place of the righteous dead.'

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'Abraham's bosom' for κόλποι Ἀβραὰμ; 'reclining' obscures this is same referent.
last_rejected.fix: and the place at Abraham's bosom, and the reclining there.
last_rejected.ruling: τὴν ἀνάκλισιν ('reclining') is a distinct item in the list, not a gloss on κόλπους Ἀβραάμ; no glossary error.

last_rejected.source_quote: ὡς ἀμφοτέρων μετὰ τῶν σωμάτων λαμβανόντων
last_rejected.why: ὡς + participle = 'on the grounds that' or 'thinking that,' not causal 'because.'
last_rejected.ruling: ὡς with participle here introduces the content of οἰομένων ('thinking that'); 'because' adequately renders the causal sense.
